subject: psychology
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 21–29 carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each) and questions 30–32 carry 4 marks (four parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: questions 33–38 carry 2 marks (30–50 words), questions 39–44 carry 3 marks (50–80 words) and questions 45–48 carry 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (i) A manager observes her team during a stressful presentation to evaluate leadership qualities. What method is she using? (ii) An interviewer uses structured questions to assess communication skills. What type of interview is this?
questions.answer: (i) Observation (a situational/observational method). (ii) Structured interview.

questions.q: Calculate: (i) IQ of a child with MA 12 and CA 8. (ii) IQ of a child with MA 10 and CA 8.
State true or false: (i) Messages that produce anxiety and fear are ineffective. (ii) Strong, personally important attitudes are hard to change.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

questions.q: Define frustration.
questions.answer: An experiential state resulting from blocking of needs and motives by external forces or the absence of a desired goal.

questions.q: What is Ritucharya?
questions.answer: Taking food and doing activities in accordance with the seasons.

questions.q: Name two interest inventories.
questions.answer: Strong Vocational Interest Blank (SVIB) and Kuder Preference Record.

questions.q: Name the four leadership styles.
questions.answer: Authoritarian, paternalistic, consultative and participative.

questions.q: Define environmental stress.
questions.answer: An undesirable transaction between the person and the environment.

questions.q: Name the five koshas.
questions.answer: Annamaya, Pranamaya, Manomaya, Vijnanamaya and Anandamaya.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the variable: (i) controlled and manipulated by the experimenter; (ii) the variable on which the impact of the IV is studied; (iii) related to personal characteristics such as age, sex and personality; (iv) related to the procedure when the participant is tested across several conditions.
questions.answer: (i) Independent variable. (ii) Dependent variable. (iii) Organismic variables. (iv) Sequential variables.

questions.q: Identify the constancy: (i) a distant car seen as the same size; (ii) a tilted plate seen as round; (iii) white paper looks white in dim light; (iv) define perceptual constancy.
questions.answer: (i) Size constancy. (ii) Shape constancy. (iii) Brightness constancy. (iv) Perception of size, shape or brightness remains the same although the retinal image changes.

questions.q: Give the effect on climate: (i) assembly line technology; (ii) aerospace technology; (iii) severe economic conditions; (iv) autonomy and feedback by managers.
questions.answer: (i) Rigid, low trust. (ii) Trust and responsibility. (iii) Threatening climate. (iv) Achievement-oriented climate.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Define personality according to Allport.
questions.answer: Personality is the dynamic organization within the individual of those psychophysical systems that determine his unique adjustment to his environment.

questions.q: Why is optimum arousal necessary for motivation?
questions.answer: Too little arousal makes us dull and relaxed, too much makes us withdraw from the goal, so a balanced level keeps us motivated.

questions.q: What is intimacy versus isolation?
questions.answer: Erikson's crisis of young adulthood: forming deep intimate relationships, especially in marriage, or becoming socially and emotionally isolated.

questions.q: What is an approach–avoidance conflict?
questions.answer: A strong tendency both to approach and to avoid the same goal, e.g. wanting to marry yet fearing loss of freedom.

questions.q: Why is leisure time important?
questions.answer: It gives mental and physical rest and a break from routine.

questions.q: What is environment?
questions.answer: The physical world and the social and cultural surroundings in which we live and interact.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe Skinner's experiment on operant conditioning.
questions.answer: A hungry rat in the Skinner Box moves randomly and accidentally presses a lever, receiving a food pellet. With repeated trials, activity centres around the lever and the rat learns that pressing it gives food; the response is reinforced and learned.

questions.q: State the achievements of the concrete operational stage.
questions.answer: Understanding of logical principles (conservation, transformation, seriation), better spatial reasoning and advanced language, but logical thinking is limited to real and concrete situations.

questions.q: Describe the negative impacts of media.
questions.answer: Spread of wrong news, rumours and propaganda leading to violence and prejudice, invasion of privacy, vulgar material and unhealthy influence on children's body image and lifestyle.

questions.q: Describe the Ayurvedic principle of Ahara.
questions.answer: Eat fresh fruits, green vegetables, beans, honey, curd and milk in balanced proportions at fixed times, chew well; vegetarian food is invigorating and prevents disease.

questions.q: Explain the greenhouse effect and its consequences.
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide, methane and CFCs trap heat, causing global warming, melting ice caps, rising sea levels, storms, flooding and agricultural disruption.

questions.q: Describe the three gunas and the three types of persons.
questions.answer: Sattwa is light (meditative, loving), Rajas is dynamism (active, restless) and Tamas is inertia (idle, lethargic). Everyone has all three; development keeps Tamas minimum.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the senses and their stimuli and organs.
questions.answer: Sight: light waves, eye; hearing: sound waves, ear; skin senses: touch, cold, warmth and pain; smell: volatile materials, nose; taste: soluble materials, tongue with four primary tastes. In addition there are vestibular (orientation) and kinesthetic (movement) senses. Thresholds determine what we detect.

questions.q: Describe the developmental tasks of adolescence given by Havighurst.
questions.answer: He listed ten tasks: mature relations with age mates, gender role, accepting physique, emotional independence, economic independence, occupation, marriage and family life, civic competence, social responsibility, and a value system. Success leads to success later; failure leads to unhappiness. Cultures differ in giving adult status.

questions.q: Explain how attitudes are formed and changed.
questions.answer: Formed by direct contact, instruction, interaction with others and observation, and by media. Change depends on source (expert, trustworthy), message (clear, fear-arousing) and person (strong attitudes resist). Congruent change is easier than incongruent.

questions.q: Discuss ability and intelligence, mental age and IQ.
questions.answer: Ability is the innate capacity to act; intelligence is its important form; Gardner holds there are multiple intelligences. Mental age comes from age scales and IQ = MA/CA x 100, with 100 average; not meaningful after 18, so ability profiles are used.
